scope: SKILL.md, api-domain, data, async-integrations, runtime-capacity, operations, verification; coverage index and L22 in meet.md. No evaluation cases, held-out tasks or grading material read.

findings.issue: Every correctness change must compare a materially different mechanism. This imposes an architecture exercise on a narrow correction whose invariant and existing mechanism are already settled.
findings.change: Require the alternative comparison when selecting or materially changing a consequential mechanism; for a local repair, retain the existing mechanism and demonstrate the counterexample and fix.

findings.issue: The entry point unconditionally loads capacity models and demands the full CPU/database/network/growth/recovery analysis, while B6 activates only for L09/L20 or a critical performance path. A bounded validation fix can therefore inherit process, surge and partition modelling it does not change.
findings.change: Apply the detailed models when workload, resource bounds or a critical path changes; otherwise preserve known limits and verify only the affected bound.

findings.issue: L22 now specifies safe telemetry transport but omits the operational signals required by meet.md: client-visible latency/useful throughput/outcomes, queue/pool/lock waits, retry amplification, saturation, lag/freshness and recovery progress. Other references measure selected experiments but do not require appropriate ongoing instrumentation.
findings.change: Extend the existing L22 mechanism cell with selection of these applicable service signals and their units/populations; verify emitted values against a controlled workload. Keep exporter resource/loss probes.

findings.issue: The every-task risk table includes reusable-skill evaluation, followed by package-local commands and fixture assertions before authoring is clearly separated. Ordinary backend work can read these as required skill trials or fixture runs despite the opening affected-responsibilities limit.
findings.change: Explicitly scope reusable-skill behavior, package commands, fixture coverage and skill-evaluation procedures to maintaining this package; keep normal application verification above that boundary.

findings.issue: Both files repeat the service-extraction decision and nearly the same release/privilege/resource/failure justification. Neither adds a distinct decision at its second occurrence.
findings.change: Keep the full local-transaction versus service-split rule in one owner and replace the other occurrence with a short cross-reference, or remove it.
